method: Model review of all 2,399 candidate headwords and supplied sense glosses in length/frequency order, with complete source records inspected for ambiguous homographs, morphology, regional/literary labels and source-quality concerns. Explicit sense choices and conservative exclusions were then serialized and checked for complete coverage, exact source-sense matches and unique accent-folded keys. This is model judgment, not native-human review. Historical mixed-country spelling Zipf scores were only a shortlist signal, not evidence of sense frequency or present-day Italy usage. A follow-up audit of approved primary glosses removed unresolved untranslated synonym and fixed-expression references; English meanings were not invented.
policy: Prefer ordinary contemporary standalone Italian words used in Italy, including familiar loanwords, standard grammatical words, lexicalized plurals, standard demonyms and established descriptive adjectives. Reject morphology-only records, name/trademark/acronym-only entries, obscure or technical homographs supported only by misleading spelling frequency, source-error cases, archaic/regional-only senses, phrase-only entries and offensive or explicit surprise answers. Select an exact eligible supplied sense rather than inventing a common missing gloss. Retain at most one answer per accent-folded key; broader guesses are unchanged.
